subject: tortoise
title: What If the First Travelers Around the Moon Weren't Human? They Were Tortoises

scenes.text: What if the first living things to circle the Moon weren't astronauts? They were two tortoises.
September 1968. The Soviet Union launches Zond 5 with two Russian tortoises, fruit fly eggs, and plants aboard.
Four days later it swings around the Moon, about 1,950 kilometers above the surface.
Three days after that, it splashes down in the Indian Ocean. No spacecraft had ever circled the Moon and come home.
The tortoises had lost about ten percent of their weight. But they were alive, and still hungry.
Three months later, Apollo 8 carried the first humans around the Moon. They were following two reptiles.

description:
What if the first earthlings to travel around the Moon were not people? In September 1968 the Soviet probe Zond 5 carried two Russian tortoises, fruit fly eggs and plants around the Moon, passing about 1,950 kilometres from the surface, and splashed down in the Indian Ocean on 21 September.
It was the first spacecraft to circle the Moon and return to Earth. The tortoises had lost about 10 percent of their body weight but showed no loss of appetite. Apollo 8 carried the first humans around the Moon three months later.
